To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

B-lymphocyte development is resistant to estrogen during fetal development but sensitive to estrogen during adulthood and that the critical developmental stage for this sensitivity occurs during the late stage of fetal liver hematopoietesis before the B-cells migrate to the bone marrow.
B-lymphocytes derived from fetal liver cells are resistant to the estrogen-mediated suppression of adult B-lymphogenesis.

the sensitivity of fetal hematopoietic progenitors to the inhibitory effects by estrogens is acquired during the final phase of fetal liver hematopoietic development, which occurs during the late stage of gestation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the estrogenic control of B-lymopoiesis during the critical developmental period of the fetus.
the developmental biology of B-lympopoiesis and the role of estrogens in the regulation of B-lymopoiesis.
the development of B-lympopoiesis and the mechanisms by which estrogens regulate this development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fetal liver cells (but not neonatal cells) are resistant to estrogen-mediated suppression of B-lympopoiesis in the adult BM micro-environment.
fetal liver cells are not resistant to estrogens, but the sensitivity of B- and T-lymphopoietic cells to estrogens increases during the final phase of their fetal liver development.
the B-lymphoid progenitor cell in the fetal liver has a unique developmental stage, which is resistant to the inhibitory effects by estrogens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

fetal liver cells are not resistant to the inhibitory effects on B-lymphogenesis of estrogens, but rather, that the sensitivity of B- lymphopoiesis to estrogens increases during the fetal development and reaches its maximum during the final phase of fetal hematopoiesis.
B-lymphocytes are not only the target cells of estrogens, but also that the sensitivity of the B-lymphocyte progenitor cell population is developmentally regulated.
fetal liver cells are resistant to estrogen and that this resistance persists into the adult life of transplanted cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensitivity of fetal liver B-lymphocytes to estrogens can be lost after transplantation into the adult bone marrow environment.
the sensitivity to estrogenic suppression is acquired by the B-lymphoid progenitors in the fetal liver, but is lost in the neonatal liver.
fetal liver hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are resistant to the inhibitory effects by estrogens in the adult microenvironment.
